description: Believes a component uses up current, so less current leaves it than enters.
example_wordings: the first bulb used up half
the bulb eats some of the current

description: Believes current splits between components in series, as it does between parallel branches.
example_wordings: each bulb gets a share of the current

description: Gets equal currents only because the components are identical, not because they are in series.
Believes adding a resistor in parallel raises total resistance.
Treats voltage and current as the same thing, or believes voltage needs current to exist.
example_wordings: no current so there is no voltage
the voltage flows through the wire

description: Believes a battery delivers the same current in any circuit.
example_wordings: the battery always gives the same current

description: Believes more resistance always means more power, ignoring what stays fixed in the circuit.
example_wordings: higher resistance means it glows more

description: Believes a thicker wire has more resistance.
example_wordings: thicker wire has more material to resist
a fat wire blocks more current
